newsitem.title: UK: IPE GAS OIL ENDS WEAKER AS BRENT FEELS IRAQ IMPACT.
newsitem.headline: IPE GAS OIL ENDS WEAKER AS BRENT FEELS IRAQ IMPACT.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed weaker on Wednesday after a slide in Brent crude futures sparked by news Baghdad plans to restart exports by the middle of August, brokers said.
Aug gas oil ended at $175.50 a tonne, down $1 from Tuesday's close. Sept Brent, meanwhile, shed 29 cents to $19.23 a barrel by 1652 GMT, above a session low posted in late afternoon trade.
"We fell back into the top of the old range and support around $19.10 held firm," said a broker.
Dealers said weak cash market sentiment was piling on the pressure, after news that a Brent cargo turning wet on Wednesday went unclaimed at the five o'clock deadline.
Oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed said on Wednesday Iraq expected to export the full $2 billion worth of oil allowed under the U.N. oil-for-food plan before the December 6 deadline.

The second phase of the deal began on June 8 but Iraq's insistence on a revised aid distribution plan delayed the restart and means it will have to export flat out to meet the interim $1 billion target by the September 5 deadline.
Rasheed said Iraq was capable of producing 2.5 million barrels per day (bpd) and exporting 1.8 million bpd.
Traders were trying to contact Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation on Wednesday to agree new contract volumes.
Brokers said U.S. inventory data showing falls in both crude and gasoline inventories were broadly neutral, although rising distillate stocks were slightly negative.
